category_title: Infrequent communicators with one-word responses who tolerate but disengage from social interaction
student_description: Charlie is a student with ASD who possesses a wide vocabulary but infrequently communicates, often relying on one-word responses and ignoring adults to pursue his own agenda. He is highly sensitive to directive communication, demands, and rushing, which immediately trigger protests and task resistance. To engage him successfully, adults must control access to motivating items, eliminate demands, and adopt a facilitative style that follows his lead and reduces the adult communication rate.

criteria.rationale: Charlie will work on his own agenda and ignore the tutor if he has free access to highly motivating items.
criteria.check: The tutor's response includes a strategy to manage or withhold access to motivating materials (e.g., keeping items out of reach, holding them) to create a natural opportunity for interaction.

criteria.rationale: Directive communication, commands, and test questions immediately trigger protests and ignoring behaviors from Charlie.
criteria.check: The tutor's response is completely free of commands, demands for compliance, or rapid-fire test questions.

criteria.rationale: Reducing the adult communication rate and labeling what Charlie is attending to gives him a sense of control and encourages him to initiate communication.
criteria.check: The tutor uses pauses to wait for the student's initiation and/or makes descriptive comments about what the student is looking at or doing, rather than redirecting his attention.
